t:
(a) 
The table of contents of chapter 31 of title 39, United States Code, is amended by striking out—


“2508. Printing of black-and-white illustrations of United States stamps.”


and inserting in lieu thereof—


“2508. Printing of black-and-white or color illustrations of United States stamps.”,



 
    (b) 
The section heading of section 2506 of title 39, United States Code, is amended to read—


“§2506. Printing of black-and-white or color illustrations of United States stamps”



 
    (c) 
Section 2506(a) of title 39, United States Code, is amended by inserting “or in color” immediately following the words “in black and white”.

fable.w: This section only makes technical amendments to the table of contents, a section heading, and the text of title 39 so that stamp illustrations may be printed in color as well as black and white. There is no tempting reading: no outside party is consulted, no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is created. Nothing crosses the federal boundary into a federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by inserting “or in color” immediately following the words “in black and white”.

qwen_block.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the table of contents and section headings of the United States Code to reflect a change in the scope of stamp printing (allowing color in addition to black-and-white). It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. The text is purely legislative housekeeping.
qwen_block.s: The table of contents of chapter 31 of title 39, United States Code, is amended by striking out—“2508. Printing of black-and-white illustrations of United States stamps.”—and inserting in lieu thereof—“2508. Printing of black-and-white or color illustrations of United States stamps.”

opus.w: This section only makes technical text changes so that stamp illustrations may be printed in color as well as black and white. No party outside the federal government is consulted or involved in any federal decision. A change to what is allowed is not the same as a process that brings outsiders into the decision.
opus.s: Section 2506(a) of title 39, United States Code, is amended by inserting “or in color” immediately following the words “in black and white”.
opus.b: The tempting reading would treat the amendment allowing "color" illustrations of stamps as a policy decision that might involve outside input. That fails because the section only makes technical edits to a heading, a table of contents and one subsection. It names no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section consists entirely of technical amendments to the table of contents and section headings of Title 39 of the U.S. Code regarding the printing of stamp illustrations. It does not establish any process for public participation, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The changes are legislative edits to statutory text, not procedural requirements for government decision-making involving non-federal parties.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing the law to allow color illustrations involves public input or consultation, but the text itself is purely a technical amendment to statutory language regarding printing specifications. It does not mention any process for public comment, advisory boards, or consultation with outside entities.
